subject: Sunridge: tailored data lifecycle attestation and TTL appeal
messages:
From: Aisha Munroe <aisha.munroe@sunridgehealth.com>
To: kimberly_park@redwood.com
Cc: Tom Rivera <tom.rivera@sunridgehealth.com>, Sunridge Health Legal <legal@sunridgehealth.com>
Date: 2026-05-14T08:12:00-07:00
Subject: Data lifecycle evidence + request for TTL variance (Sunridge account)

Hi Kimberly,

Thanks again for the demo last week. As part of our procurement / security intake we need a short attestation and evidence package for data retention and deletion practices, specifically tied to ephemeral/debug traces and tenant-scoped logs. Our security team flagged two items: (1) the default 30-day deletion window for debug/trace artifacts — we need to confirm if Sunridge can have a 90‑day window as an exception, and (2) controls/evidence around key management and proof-of-delete for tenant-scoped debug exports.

Attached is our SIG questionnaire (we filled the customer side where possible) — can your security team complete the provider sections and include:
- A sample proof-of-delete workflow for a tenant-scoped debug export
- KMS key rotation screenshots or exportable logs showing rotation history (redacted as needed)
- A packaged evidence bundle with sample log retention metadata (timestamps, S3/object lifecycle policy snippet)

Short timeline request: can you provide the completed SIG/CAIQ sections and an evidence bundle within 5 business days? Also let me know if Sunridge needs a contractual addendum to make the 90‑day TTL exception binding.

Thanks,
Aisha Munroe
Head of Security Ops | Sunridge Health
A: 415-555-0128

Attachment: sunridge_sig_questions_v2.pdf
From: kimberly_park@redwood.com <kimberly_park@redwood.com>
To: Aisha Munroe <aisha.munroe@sunridgehealth.com>
Cc: ben_carter@redwood.com, irene_choi@redwood.com, jordan_blake@redwood.com
Date: 2026-05-14T10:04:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Data lifecycle evidence + request for TTL variance (Sunridge account)

Aisha — thanks for the clear ask and the SIG file. Looping in Ben (security lead), Irene (legal ops) and Jordan (CS) so we can coordinate deliverables.

Quick notes / proposed next steps:
- We can complete the provider sections of the SIG/CAIQ and provide the evidence bundle you requested.
- For the 90-day TTL ask on debug/trace artifacts: this is feasible as a customer-specific retention profile but will require a short form addendum to the Master Services Agreement (MSA) so we can record the commitment and any risk/controls adjustments. Irene, can you advise on template and turnaround?
- Ben / Security to assemble: proof-of-delete workflow, KMS rotation evidence (redacted), sample retention metadata export and lifecycle policy snippet, and a short write-up mapping to SOC 2 controls. We’ll stage artifacts on a secure shared drive and share a download package.

Can you confirm whether Sunridge wants the 90-day window applied to:
1) ephemeral debug traces only, or
2) ephemeral debug traces plus tenant-scoped request/response logs (which have higher sensitivity)?

If you confirm option (1), we’ll prioritize. We aim to have a draft evidence bundle and completed SIG provider fields within 4 business days.

— Kimberly Park
Director, Product Security | Redwood Inference
Phone: (650) 555-0193

Attachment: retention-evidence-20260514.zip (placeholder; will be uploaded to shared drive)
From: ben_carter@redwood.com <ben_carter@redwood.com>
To: kimberly_park@redwood.com, jordan_blake@redwood.com
Cc: irene_choi@redwood.com
Date: 2026-05-14T13:20:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Data lifecycle evidence + request for TTL variance (Sunridge account)

Kimberly / Jordan — my draft inputs and evidence plan below; paste as provider responses into the SIG/CAIQ.

Provider responses (high-level):
- Default retention: production telemetry and tenant-scoped request/response logs: 30 days. Ephemeral debug traces (development/debug artifacts): configurable per-customer with a 30–90 day window subject to contractual addendum and a documented compensating control set.
- Compensating controls for 90-day debug TTL: tenant-scoped access controls (RBAC), tokenized identifiers for debug payloads, anomaly detection alerting on unusual access, and mandatory escalation/approval flow for retention extension requests.
- Proof-of-delete workflow:
  1) Customer support or CS files a retention exception request in the compliance portal.
  2) Orchestration job marks target objects for delete and emits a pre-delete manifest (object ids + checksum).
  3) Delete job executes and emits a post-delete manifest.
  4) We store manifests in a write-once S3 prefix for 180 days; manifests include deletion timestamps and deletion job run logs.
  5) On request we export manifests and provide redacted S3 object keys and checksums for verification.
- KMS evidence: we can provide key policy snippets, a redacted key rotation log (Cloud KMS audit entries showing rotation events), and a screenshot of our CMK configuration in the customer KMS project.
- Proof artifacts to deliver: pre/post-delete manifests (redacted), lifecycle policy snippet, example S3 object metadata CSV, redacted KMS rotation log, SOC 2 control mapping doc (one-pager).

Constraints / notes:
- We cannot produce raw object payloads containing PHI/PII; all artifacts will be redacted to identifiers and checksums.
- For tenant-scoped request/response logs (if included in the 90d ask), legal will require stronger contractual language and an updated data processing addendum; that will add ~7–10 business days to sign-off.

I’ll assemble the bundle and upload to the secure drive. Target to share link + completed SIG fields by EOD Wednesday (2026-05-19).

— Ben Carter
Senior Security Engineer | Redwood Inference

Date: 2026-05-15T10:03:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Data lifecycle evidence + request for TTL variance (Sunridge account)

Kimberly / Ben — thank you for the quick turnaround and the clear approach. Sunridge confirms: we only need the 90-day exception applied to ephemeral debug traces (option 1). We do NOT want tenant-scoped request/response logs included in the extension.

Next asks:
- Can you confirm the estimated delivery timeline (Ben suggested EOD Wednesday 2026-05-19) — that timeline works for our intake if the artefact package includes the one-pager mapping to SOC 2 controls and the redacted pre/post-delete manifests.
- Legal (Tom) asked whether a short MSA addendum or a signed attestation document would suffice for our procurement team. If possible, provide a short attestation template we can sign — Tom, please advise if you'd prefer DocuSign.

We’ve attached our compliance intake doc for reference. Once we have the artifacts, we’ll route to our InfoSec and Legal for final sign-off.

Best,
Aisha

Attachment: sunridge_compliance-intake.docx
